newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER TAKE FIELD WITHOUT INCE OR SFORZA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER TAKE FIELD WITHOUT INCE OR SFORZA.

text.p: Internazionale take the field against Parma in the final Serie A match of the season on Sunday without either England's Paul Ince or Swiss Ciriaco Sforza in the midfield.
Ince has been called up for England's World Cup qualifier against Poland on Saturday while Sforza has been ruled out by a persistent shin problem.
Inter, third in the league and only two points behind second-placed Parma, could still either overtake or join the north-eastern club in the battle for Italy's second Champions League spot.

Juventus, beaten 3-1 by Borussia Dortmund in this week's European Cup final, wrapped up the league title last week in a 1-1 draw at Atalanta which assured them of a return to Europe's premier football competition next season.
Inter need to win in Bologna and then hope that Parma come unstuck away to already relegated Verona.
If Inter defeat Bologna and Parma only draw with Verona, then the two sides would be level on 61 points and face each other in a playoff for the second Champions League place.
Bologna, however, also have slim European hopes riding on Sunday's game.
With fourth-placed Lazio, fith-placed Sampdoria and either Inter or Parma already certain of UEFA Cup qualification, there is only one more UEFA spot up for grabs on the final day.
Sixth-placed Udinese are in pole position to take that place as they are three points clear of Bologna.
If they lose to Roma on Sunday, however, and Bologna defeat Internazionale, then Bologna would join Udinese on 51 points and enter a play-off with Udinese.

Inter will again be led by stand-in coach Luciano Castellini, who replaced Roy Hodgson following the Englishman's resignation last week after the Milan club's defeat by German side Schalke 04 in the UEFA Cup final.
"What I need on Sunday in Bologna is a battling side but I've lost Ince, the player best suited to the purpose," he said.
In the absence of both Ince and forza, Castellini could opt for an unusual midfield of France's Jocelyn Angloma, Argentine Javier Zanetti, Dutchman Aron Winter and Salvatore Fresi.
Maurizio Ganz and Chilean Ivan Zamorano lead the Inter attack while Fabio Galante steps in to partner Massimo Paganin in central defence.
Bologna also have problems with midfielder Cristiano Scapolo, defender Amedeo Mangone and Swedish striker Kennet Andersson all suspended.
Bologna have appealed against Andersson's suspension and hope a disciplinary committee sitting on Friday will lift the ban on the Swede.

If Andersson is allowed to play, he will be partnered by Marco Schenardi and Davide Fontolan in attack, while Massimo Brambilla replaces Scapolo in midfield and Marco De Marchi replaces Mangone in defence.
